newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia's Hun Sen ready to take on ASEAN at golf.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Hun Sen ready to take on ASEAN at golf.

text.p: Cambodian Second Prime Minister Hun Sen has been taking golf lessons and is ready to take on top leaders of other Southeast Asian nations, where the game has built up a passionate following among the powerful.
Cambodia hopes to join the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) in July and golfing ability among national leaders is almost a prerequisite for membership of the influential body.
Hun Sen, speaking to reporters at his "Tiger's Lair" country residence on Monday night, said he had a full set of golf clubs and two golf buggies, which were seen in his yard.
"In 1995, I visited Malacca, Malaysia and I started to learn how to play golf," he said, adding: "I've been thinking of who can beat me among the heads of government and state of ASEAN."
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam, while Burma hopes to join later this year.
He reckoned Thailand's Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, Singapore Premier Goh Chok Tong and President Fidel Ramos of the Philippines would humble him on the greens and fairways.

He was not sure about his Malaysian counterpart Mahathir Mohamad but said, "At least I will win over the prime minister of Laos or the prime minister of Vietnam or (Indonesian) President Suharto -- he's old and cannot have a good swing. I'm still young so I can still have a very good swing."
But Hun Sen, who recently celebrated his 45th birthday, said he would be dreadful at another favourite pastime of ASEAN leaders -- karaoke -- as he could not sing.

Cambodia's only golf course was turned into a military training camp after a 1970 coup and later ploughed over, but Taiwan investors have been building a new course east of Phnom Penh and the first nine holes are in operation.
Other courses are in the pipeline, while a major hotel in the capital welcomes diplomats and officials to a driving range.
